title: Stop Illegal Entry Act of 2025
official_title: To amend the Immigration and Nationality Act to increase penalties for individuals who illegally enter and reenter the United States after being removed, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Bice (R-OK) with 5 cosponsors; passed the Republican-majority House. New mandatory-minimum immigration penalties would need 60 votes in the Senate and are likely to draw unified Democratic opposition, making passage unlikely.
summary: Raises criminal penalties for illegally entering the U.S. and adds mandatory minimum prison terms for people who reenter after being removed, especially those with prior crimes.
brief: Increases penalties for illegal entry and adds mandatory minimums for reentry after removal.

top_lines.headline: Illegal Entry Penalties
subs: Maximum prison term for illegal entry raised from 2 to 5 years
New 5-year mandatory minimum for entry plus a later serious crime

top_lines.headline: Reentry After Removal
subs: Base reentry penalty up to 10 years
Up to 15 years for those with 3+ prior misdemeanors
10-year-to-life mandatory minimum for serious prior offenses

items.main: Names the Act the “Stop Illegal Entry Act”.
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Commission of Crimes by Aliens Unlawfully Present

items.main: Raises the maximum penalty for illegal entry and adds a mandatory minimum when entry is followed by a serious crime.
items.detail: Amends Section 275 of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1325). The maximum prison term for illegal entry rises from 2 years to 5 years. A new provision imposes a mandatory minimum of 5 years (up to life) on someone who illegally enters, eludes inspection, or enters by misrepresentation and is later convicted of any crime punishable by more than one year.

sections.label: Section 3 — Increased Penalties for Reentry of Removed Alien

items.main: Restructures the penalties for reentering the U.S. after removal, adding mandatory minimums.
items.detail: Amends Section 276 of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1326). The base penalty for reentry after removal is up to 10 years; up to 15 years applies for those previously convicted of 3 or more drug or violent misdemeanors; and a 10-year-to-life mandatory minimum applies to those previously convicted of an aggravated felony, another felony, or any crime punishable by more than one year, or convicted of reentry at least twice before. Authority shifts from the Attorney General to the Secretary of Homeland Security.

gaps: The bill raises penalties but does not address the immigration court backlog that affects how quickly removal cases are resolved.
It adds mandatory minimums but provides no additional funding for detention or prosecution.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Harris
featured_quotes.text: I applaud my colleague, Representative Knott, for bringing forth this important legislation. Mr. Speaker, if we reward illegals for breaking our laws, we cannot be surprised when it continues to happen. We all know under the Biden administration, illegal immigrants were welcomed with open arms. They were given hotel rooms, cell phones, plane tickets, and work authorization. I am glad to report those days are over.

featured_quotes.name: Ms. Jayapal
featured_quotes.text: This bill is Republicans' latest attempt to scapegoat and fearmonger about immigrants. With President Trump's poll numbers tanking on immigration due to his kidnapping and disappearing of immigrants and U.S. citizens off our streets, House Republicans are, once again, looking to turn the conversation back to immigration and the border.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Correa
featured_quotes.text: there are many marines right now whose parents are undocumented who are ready to lay down their lives for this country. My colleagues on the other side of the aisle, let's work on immigration reform. This does nothing to strengthen our country or our national defense. It hurts our economy. Why are we going down this path? Let's get serious about immigration reform. Let's pass some laws that enable workers to work legally and let employers hire these workers legally, as well.

featured_quotes.name: Mrs. Bice
featured_quotes.text: Let me first start by saying I think it is rich that we stand here on the House floor and are lectured by the other side of the aisle about immigration issues when they had the last 4 years to actually address this problem. They want to deflect, as my colleague from Kansas mentioned. Let's talk about all the other things that have been happening in the country instead of the actual issue at hand. Under the Biden administration, over 10 million illegal immigrants entered this country.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Kennedy
featured_quotes.text: For too long, open-border policies have left American families at risk. Under the Biden administration, the vast majority of those charged with illegal reentry already had criminal records. In Utah, we have seen the consequences firsthand. This July in Salt Lake County, a 43-year-old Mexican national was sentenced for drug trafficking and illegal reentry. He had been deported three times before. When he was arrested, he carried an illegal firearm and more than 9,000 fentanyl pills.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Moore
featured_quotes.text: I had some prepared remarks, but as I have talked about this and looked at it even more, this is probably one of the most commonsense bills that will come before this Congress. This bill simply says if someone reenters or if someone commits a felony, that this law applies. These comments from the other side to try to confuse this issue, to misrepresent the issue, make no sense.

added: Mandatory minimums for illegal entry followed by a serious crime (5 years to life) and for reentry after removal with serious priors (10 years to life)
modified: Maximum penalty for illegal entry (8 U.S.C. 1325) raised from 2 years to 5 years; reentry penalties (8 U.S.C. 1326) restructured
Short title changed to "Stop Illegal Entry Act of 2025" (was "Stop Illegal Entry Act")
removed: Dropped a second trigger for the 10-year mandatory-minimum reentry penalty — an alien "convicted under this section at least 2 times before such removal or departure" no longer qualifies on that basis (the prior-conviction-of-listed-crimes trigger remains)
